name: Iceland
summary: Moderate, simple regime: a flat 22% on capital gains and dividends, no wealth tax, and a flat 10% inheritance tax above a small per-estate allowance (ISK 6.79m in 2026). Advance inheritance during life is also 10% with no allowance. EEA member, so EU citizens can move freely; no investor visa.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Full tax liability on worldwide income; no special regime for wealthy new arrivals.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident after staying in Iceland more than 183 days in any 12-month period, from the arrival date.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains on shares and other investments are capital income taxed at a flat 22%. A combined ISK 300,000 annual allowance (per person) covers interest, dividends and listed-share gains. Gains on a residential home owned more than two years are exempt.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: ISK 300,000 per person (ISK 600,000 per couple) combined allowance for interest, dividends and gains on listed shares (2026). Residential property held over 2 years exempt.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: No inflation indexation of gains. No exit tax on emigration was found; instead, former residents remain fully tax liable for 3 years after leaving unless they prove tax liability elsewhere.
open_questions: Confirm whether gains on foreign listed shares fall within the ISK 300,000 allowance (only relevant for small amounts).
capital_gains.rate_basis: Flat 22% capital income tax (fjármagnstekjuskattur) on nominal gains; allowance negligible for large gains.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains from business activity (including trading as a business) are taxed as business income at progressive rates up to 46.29% (2026 top bracket for individuals); passive investors stay at 22%.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: No holding-period relief for shares; residential property exempt after 2 years.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide income; foreign tax credit under treaties.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at a flat 22% capital income tax, with foreign withholding credited under treaties.
dividends.important_exceptions: For a working owner of an unlisted company, Icelandic rules can recharacterise part of distributions as wages (higher rates) - check for a private business stake. 2026: leftover personal allowance can no longer be used against capital income tax.

sources.title: Skattabreytingar á árinu 2026
sources.publisher: Government of Iceland (Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs)

open_questions: Wage-recharacterisation rules for working shareholders of private companies not verified in detail.
dividends.rate_basis: Flat 22% on gross dividends; foreign WHT credited up to the Icelandic tax.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 20% WHT on dividends to non-resident individuals and companies (PwC), reduced by treaty.
dividends.treaty_network: Moderate: about 45 treaties in force (PwC table lists 47 entries, apparently counting Czechia twice); includes the US and all major EU states.
dividends.holding_company_notes: CIT 20%; company-level participation relief exists but was not verified here; company tax kept separate.

wealth_tax.summary: Iceland has no net wealth tax (the temporary wealth tax ended after 2014). Municipalities levy property tax on real estate, which is not a wealth tax.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal property tax on real estate; rates set by each municipality (not verified).

inheritance.summary: Inheritance tax of 10% on the estate's taxable base above ISK 6,789,790 (2026, per estate, shared among heirs by inheritance share). Advance inheritance (lifetime transfers to heirs) is taxed at 10% on the full value with no allowance.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: ISK 6,789,790 per estate (deaths in 2026; 2025: ISK 6,498,129), indexed to CPI. Surviving spouse exempt.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Parliamentary resolutions to abolish the tax have been tabled but not passed.

sources.title: Skattabreytingar á árinu 2026
sources.publisher: Government of Iceland (Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs)

open_questions: Whether ordinary gifts to children outside the advance-inheritance procedure are taxed as income of the recipient (likely) was not verified.
Scope for foreign assets of an Icelandic-domiciled deceased (worldwide presumed) not confirmed on an official page.
inheritance.gift_tax: Advance inheritance to heirs is taxed at a flat 10% of the full value (no allowance, debts not deductible). Other gifts are not covered by inheritance tax and may be taxable income of the recipient (unverified).
inheritance.foreign_assets: Heirs are taxed on all valuables received when an estate is settled in Iceland; Icelandic real estate is taxed regardless of the deceased's residence.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Estates are settled where the deceased was domiciled; no citizenship-based tail found.
inheritance.spouse_note: If assets pass to a surviving spouse or cohabitant, no inheritance tax is levied (Act 14/2004 on inheritance tax; PwC).

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if staying more than 183 days in any 12-month period (or domiciled in Iceland). Former residents remain fully liable for 3 years after leaving unless they prove tax liability elsewhere.

routes.name: EEA free movement
routes.requirements: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens may live in Iceland and register with Registers Iceland.

routes.name: Residence permit
routes.requirements: No investor visa; non-EEA nationals need a permit on work, family or other grounds. Not verified in detail.

corporate.summary: CIT 20% (unchanged for 2026). Dividend WHT 20% to non-residents, reduced by treaty.

sources.title: Skattabreytingar á árinu 2026
sources.publisher: Government of Iceland (Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs)

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median asking rent of the 8 capital-area listings (Reykjavík, Garðabær, Hafnarfjörður) with 4-5 bedrooms on the first results page of Igloo (myigloo.is) on 2026-10-15 (ISK 400,000-695,000; 57 listings nationwide with 4+ bedrooms). Large houses of 170-240 m² asked ISK 525,000-695,000. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

intl_school_annual_fee.description: Iceland's only IB Diploma programme is at Menntaskólinn við Hamrahlíð (MH), a public upper-secondary school with no tuition. Annual cost of the 2-year Diploma = MH fee ISK 15,000 per semester (ISK 30,000 a year) + IB exam and materials fees ISK 160,000 over the programme (ISK 80,000 a year), as on the school's fee page (updated 25.09.2026). The private International School of Iceland stops at Grade 10 and does not publish fees.

cost_of_living.notes: Health insurance, housekeeper and price per m² not sourced. The school figure reflects a free public IB programme, which makes Reykjavik look cheap on schooling; there is no private international secondary school.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain US-taxed; Iceland-US treaty (2007) applies with saving clause.
open_questions: Gift taxation outside advance inheritance unverified.
